message.content:
Yes—most vehicles let you crank the engine even though the doors are locked and the parking‑brake is still engaged.  
Here’s what usually happens:

| Step | What you’ll see / feel |
|------|------------------------|
| **Unlock** your driver’s side (or use the key fob/remote start button). | Doors open automatically once the ignition cycle begins. |
| **Release the parking brake** (if your car requires manual release before cranking). | Some models won’t allow the starter motor to engage unless the parking brake is off. |
| **Start the engine** – turn the key or push “start.” | Engine turns over normally; no impact on the locks or brakes. |

If your car has a *remote‑start* feature, you can simply hit the remote start button from anywhere inside the house. That will power up the engine without physically opening the doors at all.

Once the engine is running, you can safely pull out the dashboard gauges or connect an OBD‑II reader to read real‑time data on fuel level, battery voltage, etc., while keeping everything secure behind closed doors.
